s1.syndrome_frame: liver lesion with cellular proliferation and abnormal histology
salient_findings: multifocal basophilic foci in the liver
polygonal to short spindle-shaped cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios
frequent mitotic figures and sparse hepatocellular necrosis
local invasion into adjacent blood vessels
key_facts: 3-week-old male Sprague-Dawley rat
housed under standard conditions
assigned to a control group in a pharmacological study
euthanized under anesthesia at 7 weeks of age
liver and other organs appeared grossly unremarkable at necropsy
serum AST and ALT levels were within normal limits
histological examination of the left lateral liver lobe
multifocal basophilic foci located predominantly in the perilobular region
tumor cells exhibited clear cell borders and hyperchromatic nuclei
narrow spaces containing erythrocytes between tumor cells
reticular fibers formed a loosely connected, irregular network within tumor cell aggregates
